APPLICATION FOR EXTENSION OF TIME TO FILE 
REPLY BRIEF ON THE MERITS 

To:  Justice  Samuel  A.  Alito,  Jr.,  Circuit  Justice  for  the  United  States 

Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit: 

Pursuant  to  Rule  30.3  of  the  Rules  of  this  Court,  Petitioner  Jane 

Cummings requests an extension of four (4) days, to and including November 

2,  2021,  in  which  to  file  her  reply  brief  on  the  merits.  In  support  of  this 

application, petitioner states: 

1.  On  July  2,  2021,  this  Court  granted  certiorari  in  this  case.  Shortly 

thereafter, the parties jointly filed a motion to extend the due dates for their 

briefs  on  the  merits.  On  July  12,  2021,  this  Court  granted  the  motion, 

extending the time in which to file the opening brief to August 23, 2021, and 

the time in which to file respondent’s brief to September 29, 2021. 

2. The reply brief is currently due on October 29, 2021, and the Court 

has scheduled argument for November 30, 2021. With the four-day requested 

extension,  the  reply  brief  would  be  due  on  November  2,  2021—four  weeks 

before oral argument and well before the completion of the previous sitting of 

arguments. 

3. This is petitioner’s first request for an extension of time on the reply 

brief, and it would not require the Court to alter the date on which the case is 

set for oral argument. 

4. This short extension is warranted because of the heavy press of other 

matters undersigned counsel is handling. Counsel of record is part of the seven-

1

lawyer  Eisenberg  & Baum  Center  for  Deaf  and  Hard  of  Hearing,  which  has 

numerous active cases across the country on short deadlines. Co-counsel at the 

Stanford  Supreme  Court  Litigation  Clinic  is  currently  short-staffed  and 

involved in several matters pending in this Court, including Hemphill v. New 

York, No. 20-637 (argued October 5, 2021), and Houston Community College 

System v. Wilson, No. 20-804 (to be argued on November 2, 2021). 

5. Counsel for respondent has consented to this extension. 

Respectfully submitted, 

By:  

Edward C. DuMont 
STANFORD LAW SCHOOL

Stanford, CA 94305
